dossier.deep_context:
# 2022-604 — Quixilver: Octopus Prime

Primary source: https://github.com/frc604/2022-public

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

Code commit: 2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d. Read the original FRC-2022 tree. FRC-2022-NEW is a learning rewrite, not certified event code. File locators: Intake.java, BallPath.java, Launcher.java, Climber.java and Calibration.java under FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/.

## Published FRC-2022 code · drivetrain

### Published construction or code

Calibration defines a 20.5-inch wheelbase and track width, 3.94-inch wheel diameter, 6.75:1 drive reduction and 12.8:1 steering reduction. These are software configuration values, not independent measurements.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Mechanical selection rationale is not established by the code.

### Engineering interpretation

The swerve and localization must be considered together. A configured maximum speed is not a demonstrated match speed. Wheel calibration affects both the path tracker and the launch-distance estimate, so a copied drive configuration can corrupt scoring even when teleop feels acceptable. Check hardware revision, encoder scales and actual loaded wheel circumference before borrowing constants.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Published FRC-2022 code · intake

### Published construction or code

Intake.java configures distinct Falcon 500 roller and deployment motors, a trapezoidal deployment profile, arm feedforward and a 45A deployment stator limit. Intake, eject, unjam and yeet commands are separate entry points.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The code does not state why this exact mechanical geometry was selected.

### Engineering interpretation

The published interface treats recovery and reverse flow as designed operating modes. That is useful architectural evidence, but it does not establish roller material, width, compression or impact survival. A profiled pivot can reduce abrupt actuation; whether it does so under contact depends on the real mechanism and controller settings. Preserve these unknowns rather than infer a later 604 polycarbonate intake in 2022.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Published FRC-2022 code · transfer

### Published construction or code

BallPath.java separates upper and lower Falcon-driven transport sections and exposes position/velocity control and sensor-based ball handling.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Exact transport geometry and team selection rationale remain unresolved.

### Engineering interpretation

Separately controlled transport can stage a second cargo while releasing the first, but introduces coordination between occupancy sensing, launcher readiness and reverse recovery. Code supports the existence of these interfaces, not an independent throughput result or proof of jam-free behavior. A two-cargo game rewards preserving a reliable staged sequence; extra transport complexity should be justified by actual scoring continuity.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Published FRC-2022 code · scoring

### Published construction or code

Launcher.java configures front and rear Falcon flywheel motors with feedforward and feedback. Readiness checks use a five-sample speed buffer and tolerance; distance-related bounds are treated separately.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The source establishes readiness logic, not a published mechanical reason for wheel geometry.

### Engineering interpretation

Requiring recent samples within tolerance is different from checking one instantaneous RPM. It can reject a momentary speed crossing after spin-up or a previous shot. The trade is delayed release versus launch consistency. The existence of front/rear motors does not establish independent spin control in competition, wheel dimensions, a turret, or exact release angle. Those require geometry and event evidence.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Published FRC-2022 code · endgame

### Published construction or code

Climber.java configures three NEO motors and staged first-rung, lift, handoff, high-rung and traversal transitions. It uses filtered tilt and tilt rate, position/profile completion and an angle-history lockout.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Comments explicitly describe gyro-controlled transitions and an antenna-touch-angle lockout; broader hardware intent is not fully documented here.

### Engineering interpretation

This is a dynamic climb sequence, not a simple winch toggle. A transition may require both operator approval and a suitable swing/position state. That ties compliance, sensor filtering, angular thresholds and operator timing together. A traversal state in released code proves intended capability, not a successful traversal in every match or that all events ran this revision. Exact hook and support geometry remain open.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Original code versus learning rewrite · controls

### Published construction or code

The repository README identifies FRC-2022 as robot code and FRC-2022-NEW as a work-in-progress reimplementation for learning and cleanup. Quikplan-swerve and the offboard quixpf particle filter are separate directories.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The rewrite is explicitly described as preparation and learning.

### Engineering interpretation

Do not read the cleaner NEW tree and retroactively claim every behavior was fielded in 2022. The original tree is the stronger starting point for event-era behavior, though its final commit still lacks per-event installation certification. Pin the repository commit and file path when citing code; preserve the distinction between software configuration, mechanical construction and observed performance.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Evidence limits

- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.

source_reviews.review_basis: Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.
source_reviews.facts: Separate Falcon-controlled roller and deployment. Deployment uses a motion profile and arm feedforward.
source_reviews.limitations: The code exposes actuation and target states. Installed geometry needs a physical source.

source_reviews.title: Ball path subsystem
source_reviews.locator: Queue, beam-break, color and launch methods
source_reviews.review_basis: Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.
source_reviews.facts: Two powered feed zones, three beam-break inputs, a color input, top/bottom possession states, and feed speed selection based on the upper beam.
source_reviews.limitations: The switch logic reports controller intent. Sensor data and field performance are separate.

source_reviews.title: Collect and move to top queue
source_reviews.review_basis: Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.
source_reviews.facts: The command acquires cargo and runs the path together. It monitors the bottom sensor and updates the upper state after a non-interrupted transfer.
source_reviews.limitations: A state transition is not independent evidence that the cargo reached its intended pose.

source_reviews.title: Launcher subsystem
source_reviews.review_basis: Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.
source_reviews.facts: Both launcher speed histories must be in tolerance. The launch mode checks feasible shot status.
source_reviews.limitations: No measured flywheel recovery or accuracy map.

source_reviews.title: Climber subsystem
source_reviews.review_basis: Static review of the FRC-2022 directory at 2cfd645d. The README separately identifies FRC-2022-NEW as a work in progress.
source_reviews.facts: The published sequence includes reaches, partial lifts and intermediate handoff states. The code accepts robot tilt and tilt-rate inputs.
source_reviews.limitations: Exact hook load paths and event-specific traverse performance remain unresolved.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Octopus Prime is a swerve cargo robot with a deployable intake, a managed two-position cargo path, two controlled launcher speeds and a staged climb. Its technical point is how the mechanism boundaries are made explicit in software. The collector changes the cargo’s state from outside the robot to present at the lower queue. The path advances it to a staged position. The shot logic waits for feasible, stable speed before feeding. Separate reverse and clearing commands show that handling a wrong or stuck cargo was part of the system.
piece_flow: The deployed roller draws cargo toward the lower path. Beam-break and color input help classify and track the piece.
The lower and upper powered rollers advance and stage it. The software moves its queue state on the transfer command’s normal completion.
When the launcher is ready, the ball path changes feed speed depending on whether cargo is already near the launcher. Empty sensor states can end the feed.
The code provides clearing and rejection behavior. During climb, the robot sequences reaches, lifts and handoffs as separate states.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The release describes functional interfaces rather than a dimensioned robot. A physical layout must place the first sensor after a useful capture contact, preserve control across the lower-to-upper transfer and keep cargo seated near the launcher without jamming it into the wheels. The intake must stow without trapping a staged ball or limiting approach. Climb states imply another envelope near the rungs and a structure that supports the chassis under suspended load.

subsystems.name: Collector
subsystems.construction: One motor runs the acquisition contact and another deploys it. The deploy actuator uses a profiled goal with gravity-related feedforward.
subsystems.operation: Select deploy or retract, then run acquisition, reverse or clearing motion as required.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team rationale is not given in the inspected subsystem.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Separate deploy and roller control lets the driver clear the ball while preserving the useful mouth pose. It also makes two failure paths possible.
subsystems.interfaces: Place the lower sensor where it can distinguish captured cargo from a ball merely passing across the mouth.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check the encoder zero after a hit and reversal when the mouth is blocked.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact contact width, bumper geometry and sensor alignment.

subsystems.name: Queue and transfer
subsystems.construction: Lower and upper powered regions have separate stored state and sensor input. Color is evaluated against an alliance-color selection.
subsystems.operation: Advance cargo to the top position and preserve separation so a second ball does not enter the shot contact early.
subsystems.team_rationale: Code comments describe staging and a different feed speed when cargo is already at the launcher.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Tracking both occupancy and color can prevent a correct launch command from feeding the wrong physical ball. The benefit depends on synchronization between sensors and stored state.
subsystems.interfaces: Upper sensor, queue location and launcher entrance need reliable spacing.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test an interrupted move while cargo spans both regions. A debounced detector may need a recovery based on the actual sensor pattern.
subsystems.unknowns: No measured jam rate, color detection accuracy or successful queue recovery data.

subsystems.name: Launch readiness
subsystems.construction: Separate launcher motor controls maintain the requested speed. Both histories are checked before readiness.
subsystems.operation: Convert computed exit velocity to a speed setting, wait for steady samples and feed once feasible.
subsystems.team_rationale: The implementation uses feasibility and a short speed history rather than a single sample.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Readiness can improve repeatability, but an overly strict settling condition can waste an open shot window. Measure the time and accuracy trade.
subsystems.interfaces: Launcher entry must retain the piece while wheels accelerate, then feed cleanly without reducing speed below the tolerance band.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare single and paired shots on a partially discharged battery. Log rejected shot conditions.
subsystems.unknowns: No independently measured recovery time or field accuracy by range.

subsystems.name: Traversal sequencing
subsystems.construction: The climb controller divides the maneuver into reaches, contact, partial lifts and handoffs with tilt inputs.
subsystems.operation: Advance through stable intermediate states while moving between rungs.
subsystems.team_rationale: Published source exposes transition structure without giving a rationale for each threshold.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A sequence is easier to recover when each load-transfer state has an observable condition. Test each intermediate state rather than only the complete routine.
subsystems.interfaces: Hooks and rung approach must keep the next reach accessible when the chassis swings under load.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check unexpected swing and early contact. Confirm the routine has a safe response when a handoff cannot be completed.
subsystems.unknowns: No dimensioned hook or rigging data in the reviewed sections.

revisions: The FRC-2022-NEW directory is a rewrite and is outside this competition-oriented source review.
transferable_principles: Define occupancy and recovery at each possession boundary.
Measure shot readiness over multiple launches and battery conditions.
Keep hardware and controller limits attached to their source snapshot.
disconfirming_conditions: Remove a transfer or independent deployment axis when it contributes little useful reach or throughput.
A less complex climb can earn more total contribution if a traversal mechanism harms the primary scoring cycle.
remaining_gaps: Physical packaging of the collector, feed and climb, tested acquisition limits, and match-level configuration history.
